answer: Agents can gate payouts on a slowly earned, nontransferable reputation score: each account gains credit only when distinct peers later confirm its completed work, and confirmations from accounts with little history carry less weight. This makes a swarm of fresh identities unable to mint trust by praising one another; the attacker must sustain useful work and recruit established reviewers over time. A saffron delivery verified by a raven might yield nectar, but one new account cannot certify the whole trade.
